Application Materials.content:
- Supporting documents usually include **evidence of qualifications (certificates or transcripts)**; evidence of English language ability, if English is not your first language; **a research proposal** (check the department website for instructions, as these vary); any department-specific additional requirements (for example, some courses ask for specific information in a **personal statement**); and you may need **two references**. Referees will be contacted and asked to submit a reference directly via the referee portal, so applicants should make referees aware in advance.
- If any certificates or transcripts have been issued in a language other than English, include official, authenticated English translations.
- The translation should be on official letter-headed paper, clearly state that it is an accurate translation of the original, and include: the translator or translation company's name and contact details; the translator or translation company's credentials or qualifications; the date of the translation; and the translator's full name and signature, or the full name and signature of an authorised official from the translation company.
- The translation should be done by an official translator/translation service. Translations by agents are not accepted unless the agency offers a recognised translation service and the translator can demonstrate appropriate credentials, for example NAATI, CATTI or NAETI.

Application Deadlines.content:
Year of entry: **2026**.
Due to high demand for this course, we operate a [staged admissions process](https://www.manchester.ac.uk/study/masters/courses/list/11424/msc-data-science-social-analytics/#staged-admissions) with multiple selection deadlines throughout the year.
**Applications for 2026 entry:**
- **Stage 1:** Application received by **7th December 2025**; Application update by **20th February 2026**
- **Stage 2:** Application received by **1st March 2026**; Application update by **1st May 2026**
- **Stage 3:** Application received by **3rd May 2026**; Application update by **19th June 2026**
- **Stage 4:** Application received by **5th July 2026**; Application update by **31st July 2026**
Applications received after our final selection deadline will be considered at our discretion if places are still available. All places are subject to availability and if you apply at one of the later stages, some courses may already be reaching capacity or be closed to further applications.

Academic Requirements.content:
**High 2:1 honours degree (or overseas equivalent).** You are expected to have a degree with a substantial proportion of social science content; as a minimum you should have completed **two degree level units** on topics from any of the following: sociology, psychology, anthropology, economics, history, human geography, political science, public health.
The following includes other skills/experience that would increase the chances of being selected:
- Evidence of applying statistical modelling to social sciences.
- Non-academic experience with the application of statistical models to social issues.
- Experience working on public policy issues or similar.
In your application, you should demonstrate aptitude, knowledge and/or interest in three areas:
- data analytics and/or statistics;
- computational subjects; and
- pathway specific requirements.
These can be demonstrated by course units taken at undergraduate level and high school level, or professional experience.
For applicants from China (Mainland): taught master's applicants with a bachelor's degree from a recognised good-quality Chinese university, with a **minimum overall average grade of 80%** or a **minimum GPA of 3.0 (out of 4.0)** will be considered for admission on to taught masters programmes; entry requirements differ between courses and applicants should refer to the entrance requirements of individual programmes for further guidance.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
Applicants whose first language is not English should meet the following language requirements:
- **IELTS Academic: 7.0 overall** with **no component below 6.5**.
- **TOEFL iBT: 100** with **no score below 22 in each section**. TOEFL code for Manchester is **0757**.
- **Pearson Test of English (PTE): 76 overall** with **no component below 70**.
**Pre-Sessional English Courses**
- Applicants who do not meet these scores may be required to complete a pre-sessional English language course at the University of Manchester prior to the start of the course.
- **6 Week Pre-Sessional Course:** **IELTS 6.5 overall** with **6.0 in each sub-skill**.
- **10 Week Pre-sessional Course:** **IELTS 6.0 overall** with **6.0 in three sub-skills, and 5.5 in no more than one sub-skill**.
- If you have not yet completed your current academic study and are interested in studying a pre-sessional course, you must hold an **IELTS for UKVI (Academic)** test certificate to ensure that you are eligible for a separate visa for the English language course.
- Some English Language test results are only valid for **two years**. Your English Language test report must be valid on the **start date of the course**.
- Applicants from [majority English-speaking countries](https://www.manchester.ac.uk/study/international/admissions/language-requirements/) (or applicants who have studied for a full bachelor's degree or higher in one of these countries) may be **exempt** from submitting further evidence of English language proficiency.

Program Overview.content:
- **Duration:** **1 year**. **Degree awarded:** MSc. **Study mode:** Full-time, in person.
- MSc Data Science (Social Analytics) is a uniquely interdisciplinary programme that brings together expertise from across Manchester’s facilities, giving you strong foundations in data science and the opportunity to collaborate across disciplines to tackle local and global challenges. The course focuses on the data techniques and uses most relevant to social analytics.
- The course prepares you for a successful career in this high-demand field by developing abilities in data analysis, project design, computational methods, and data stewardship. It aims to train you to ask important research questions, evaluate the quality of available evidence, select appropriate methods, and use analytical skills to visualise, interpret and provide strategic advice and insight.
- The programme welcomes applicants from a range of STEM, business and humanities backgrounds, allowing it to create a diverse cohort and enrich discussions around the uses and potential of data.
- Special features include an interdisciplinary approach spanning Statistics, Demography, Social Networks, Data Science, Economics, Politics, Criminology, Health, Sociology, and other fields, and hands-on experience analysing real-world data using R, Python, SQL, Excel and other tools.
- The course is taught by an interdisciplinary team through lectures, computer based practicals, e-learning, workshops, student presentations, group work, and individual research.
- A master’s degree is formed of 180 credits. 120 credits are made up by a mix of mandatory and optional course units, and the remaining 60 credits are awarded through a compulsory research component in the form of an **8500-word extended research project**. The project mirrors a real-world data science investigation, including replication code and an accompanying overview video for stakeholders, and is supported by weekly research methodology lectures.
- Graduates develop a highly valued skillset for careers in policy, business, research and more. Previous students have gone on to roles such as data scientists, civil servants, consultants, researchers, entrepreneurs, and in AI. Career paths include banking and financial services, charities and research organisations, the Civil Service, the IT and tech sector, business management, high performance sports analysis, large retail chains, and the pharmaceutical industry.
- The course is eligible for the fully-funded 1+3 studentship offered by the ESRC North West Social Sciences Doctoral Training Partnership (NWSSDTP), offering a route from master’s-level study into postgraduate research and PhD study. [Find out more on the 1+3 ESRC NWSSDTP webpage](https://www.humanities.manchester.ac.uk/study/postgraduate-research/funding/list-of-awards/1-3-esrc-nwssdtp/#:~:text=Open%20to%20applicants%20from%20all,structured%20pathway%20into%20postgraduate%20research.).
- The University of Manchester is one of the UK’s most targeted universities by top graduate employers, and students have access to the dedicated [Careers Service](https://www.careers.manchester.ac.uk/) during the course and for two years after graduation.

Curriculum.content:
- **Duration:** **1 year**. **MSc | Full-time: In person**.
- A master’s degree is formed of **180 credits**. **120** of these credits are made up by a mix of mandatory and optional course units, worth **15 credits each**. You will need to select **eight** of these course units, with **60 credits taken each semester**.
- The core units are:
- Machine Learning and Statistics (both semesters)
- Understanding Databases
- Understanding Data and their Environment
- Applying Data Science
- The remaining **60 credits** are awarded through a compulsory research component in the form of an **8500-word extended research project**. Your project will mirror a real-world data science investigation, including replication code and an accompanying overview video for stakeholders. Your dissertation must be within the area of one of the course units you have chosen. The extended research project is supported by weekly research methodology lectures designed to improve your academic, research and writing skills.
- Optional course units range from statistical foundations to social network modelling and policy inferences. The course unit details given below are subject to change.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
- If your **School or Department Admissions Team agrees** to your request to defer, you may do so **without paying a deposit**.
- If you’ve already paid the deposit and then decide to defer, your payment will be **carried over** and used towards your tuition fees for the new entry year.
- If the **CAS deposit increases** for your new entry year, you’ll need to **pay the difference** before your new CAS can be issued.
